title: PandaOmics AI platform prioritizes ALS targets, eight validated in a Drosophila model
summary: The AI-driven target-discovery platform PandaOmics analysed expression data from CNS samples (237 cases, 91 controls) and iPSC-derived motor neurons (135 cases, 31 controls), proposing 17 high-confidence and 11 novel therapeutic targets. In a c9ALS Drosophila model, suppression of eight previously unreported genes (KCNB2, KCNS3, ADRA2B, NR3C1, P2RY14, PPP3CB, PTPRC, RARA) strongly rescued eye neurodegeneration. The fly eye model is a limited readout, inputs are public omics data and the abstract does not give a hit rate versus a random baseline.
ai_technology: PandaOmics AI-driven target-discovery platform scoring and ranking therapeutic targets from expression data

evidence.tested: In vivo screen of AI-prioritized targets in a c9ALS Drosophila model.
evidence.unknown: Hit rate versus random baseline; the platform's specific machine-learning operations; relevance to human disease; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: An AI target-discovery platform ranked genes from ALS expression data to select targets for the fly screen.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
